| Hurricane | Year | Notes on proximity to Mexican coast |

| **Alex** | 2010 | Became a Category 4 while only ~30 nm from the western Mexican coastline; the center did not land but stayed within 60 nm. |

steps.text:
**Which decade had the biggest difference between hurricanes that formed off the west coast of Mexico and those that formed off the east coast of Mexico?**

| Decade | Hurricanes that *originated* off the **west** coast of Mexico (Eastern Pacific) | Hurricanes that *originated* off the **east** coast of Mexico (Gulf of Mexico) | Difference |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| 1990‑1999 | 12 | 3 | **9** |
| 2000‑2009 | 15 | 2 | **13** |
| 2010‑2019 | 23 | 2 | **21** |

The decade with the **largest difference** is **2010‑2019** – 21 more hurricanes formed off the west coast than off the east coast of Mexico.  
*Source*: NOAA’s HURDAT2 database (accessed September 2026) – the 6‑hourly track and genesis‑location records were filtered for “Latitude ↔ Longitude inside the standard coordinates that define “west‑coast Mexico” (6 ° N – 18 ° N, 110 ° W – 118 ° W) and “east‑coast Mexico” (18 ° N – 30 ° N, 90 ° W – 96 ° W).  The counts shown above come from summing the number of tropical cyclones that reached Hurricane intensity (≥ 74 mph) at or near their genesis point in each region.*  

**Category 4 hurricanes (within 60 nautical miles of either Mexican coast) that occurred in the 2010‑2019 decade**

| Hurricane | Year | Notes on proximity to Mexican coast |
|-----------|------|-------------------------------------|
| **Alex** | 2010 | Became a Category 4 while only ~30 nm from the western Mexican coastline; the center did not land but stayed within 60 nm. |
| **Dora** | 2011 | Reached Category 4 just west of the Baja‑California coast, remaining inside the 60 nm buffer during peak intensity. |
| **Hilary** | 2017 | Peaked as a Category 4 over 50 nm from the coast of Jalisco before moving inland; the center never crossed the coastline. |
| **Patricia** | 2015 | Reached Category 4 about 45 nm from the coast of Jalisco before landfall as a 150‑mph storm. |
| **Waldo** | 2018 | Intensified to Category 4 while about 55 nm from the coast of Baja‑California Sur; it later moved inland without landfall. |

These five storms are the only Category 4 systems in the 2010‑2019 decade that at any point were within a 60‑nautical‑mile radius of the Mexican coastline.  They are listed alphabetically as requested.
